issues.legal_issue: A statutory process for removing a religious institution’s head, including suspension during an inquiry, does not violate equality or the right to hold and enjoy property when it is based on misconduct or unfitness and includes procedural safeguards.
material_facts: The officeholder faced charges concerning alleged misappropriation and defalcation of trust funds, as well as leading an immoral life.
He was suspended while the charges were investigated.
The inquiry was quasi-judicial, and an order of removal could be challenged in court, with a further appeal to the High Court.
The suspension was intended to prevent interference with evidence or other conduct that could defeat the inquiry.
issues.conclusion: The challenged removal and suspension provisions imposed reasonable restrictions in the interest of the general public and did not violate Articles 14 or 19(1)(f) of the Constitution.
issues.legal_principle: Under Articles 14 and 19(1)(f), restrictions must be reasonable and in the interest of the general public. A head of a math holds property subject to duties as a trustee and may be removed for relevant misconduct or incapacity. The Court relied on The Commissioner, Hindu Religious Endowments, Madras v. Sri Lakshmindra Thirtha Swamiar of Shirur Mutt, [1954] S.C.R. 1005, and H. H. Sudhundra Thirtha Swamiar v. Commissioner for Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments, Mysore, [1963] Supp. 2 S.C.R. 302. It held that changing the removal procedure to a quasi-judicial inquiry, subject to court review and appeal, was not unconstitutional, and that suspension during the inquiry was a necessary and reasonable safeguard.

rule.if: constitutional_validity_challenge and charges_concern_unfitness_or_trust_misconduct and officeholder_suspended_during_inquiry and inquiry_has_review_safeguards

predicates.constitutional_validity_challenge: A person challenged the constitutionality of a process for removing or suspending the head of a religious institution.
predicates.charges_concern_unfitness_or_trust_misco: The officeholder faced charges concerning incapacity, failure to perform duties, breach of trust, misuse of institutional property, or other relevant misconduct.
predicates.officeholder_suspended_during_inquiry: The authority suspended the officeholder while an inquiry into the charges was pending.
predicates.inquiry_has_review_safeguards: The authority conducted a quasi-judicial inquiry, and the resulting removal decision could be challenged in court with a further appeal available.

issues.definition: When a constitutional challenge concerns removal for unfitness or trust-related misconduct, and suspension occurs during an inquiry with review safeguards, the removal and suspension framework is treated as constitutionally valid.

issues.legal_issue: Temporarily preventing a religious officeholder from performing the office does not violate the freedom to practise and propagate religion when the person remains able to enter the religious institution and is not barred from religious practice.
material_facts: The officeholder was suspended pending an inquiry and another official was placed in charge of day-to-day administration.
Although police guarded the institution, the officeholder was not prohibited from entering it.
The record did not establish that he was barred from professing, practising, or propagating his religion.
issues.conclusion: The arrangement did not violate the officeholder’s right under Article 25(1) to profess, practise, and propagate religion.
issues.legal_principle: Article 25(1) protects the freedom to profess, practise, and propagate religion. The Court held that the right was not infringed because the officeholder had not been prohibited from entering the institution or exercising that freedom there.

predicates.constitutional_validity_challenge: A person challenged an arrangement affecting the exercise of religious freedom.
predicates.religious_officeholder_temporarily_sidel: An authority temporarily prevented the religious officeholder from managing or administering the institution.
predicates.entry_to_religious_site_remained_permitt: The officeholder remained permitted to enter the religious institution.
predicates.religious_practice_not_barred: The authority did not prohibit the officeholder from professing, practising, or propagating the religion.

issues.definition: When a religious officeholder is temporarily sidelined but may still enter the institution and is not barred from religious practice, the freedom to profess, practise, and propagate religion is not infringed.

issues.legal_issue: A temporary administrative arrangement does not violate a religious denomination’s autonomy over rites and ceremonies when neither the governing law nor the appointed administrator interferes with deciding or performing those rites and ceremonies.
material_facts: An official was appointed temporarily to attend to the day-to-day administration of the institution and its endowments while the officeholder was suspended.
The officeholder alleged interference with the denomination’s religious autonomy.
Nothing in the challenged provisions empowered the authority to decide which rites and ceremonies were essential to the religion.
No interference with such matters by the authority or the temporary administrator was established.
issues.conclusion: There was no contravention of Article 26(b), because the denomination’s autonomy concerning rites and ceremonies had not been interfered with.
issues.legal_principle: Article 26(b) protects a religious denomination’s autonomy in deciding what rites and ceremonies are essential according to its tenets. Relying on The Commissioner, Hindu Religious Endowments, Madras v. Sri Lakshmindra Thirtha Swamiar of Shirur Mutt, [1954] S.C.R. 1005, the Court held that neither the statutory powers nor their exercise in this case interfered with that autonomy.

predicates.constitutional_validity_challenge: A religious denomination challenged a state arrangement as interfering with its religious autonomy.
predicates.temporary_administrator_appointed: An authority appointed an administrator temporarily to manage the institution’s day-to-day affairs.
predicates.no_interference_with_rites_or_ceremonies: Neither the governing arrangement nor the administrator interfered with the denomination’s decisions about or performance of religious rites and ceremonies.

issues.definition: When an administrator is appointed temporarily but does not interfere with the denomination’s rites or ceremonies, its ritual autonomy is not violated.

issues.legal_issue: A temporary arrangement for administering religious institutional property does not violate a denomination’s right to administer that property when the arrangement responds to a specified temporary need and does not permanently transfer the right of administration.
material_facts: The officeholder was suspended pending an inquiry into serious charges of misappropriation and defalcation of trust funds and leading an immoral life.
An official was appointed temporarily to manage the institution and its endowments during the inquiry.
The statutory arrangement applied to specified temporary circumstances and lasted only until the relevant disability ceased or another officeholder succeeded.
The arrangement did not permanently vest administration in an authority lacking entitlement under the institution’s customary rules.
issues.conclusion: The temporary administrative arrangement did not contravene Article 26(d).
issues.legal_principle: Article 26(d) protects a religious denomination’s right to administer property according to law, subject to lawful regulation. The Court relied on The Commissioner, Hindu Religious Endowments, Madras v. Sri Lakshmindra Thirtha Swamiar of Shirur Mutt, [1954] S.C.R. 1005, which distinguished a drastic power exercisable without justifying necessity from a limited arrangement for specified circumstances. It also referred to H. H. Sudhundra Thirtha Swamiar v. Commissioner for Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments, Mysore, [1963] Supp. 2 S.C.R. 302, in discussing the officeholder’s duties as trustee. The temporary arrangement did not take administration away altogether or vest it permanently in another authority.

rule.if: constitutional_validity_challenge and temporary_administrative_need_exists and administration_is_only_temporary and administration_is_not_permanently_transferred

predicates.constitutional_validity_challenge: A religious denomination challenged a state arrangement affecting administration of its property.
predicates.temporary_administrative_need_exists: A temporary vacancy, suspension, succession dispute, or comparable circumstance created a need for an interim administrative arrangement.
predicates.administration_is_only_temporary: The interim administrator’s authority lasts only until the temporary circumstance ends or a successor takes office.
predicates.administration_is_not_permanently_transf: The arrangement does not permanently vest the denomination’s right of administration in an authority not entitled to exercise it under the institution’s customary rules.

issues.definition: When a temporary need justifies an interim arrangement that ends with the temporary circumstance and does not permanently transfer administration, the denomination’s property-administration right is not abrogated.
